headline: IIT Convocation speaker clarifies that 'Bharat is a responsibility' applies to every student's unpaid duty to organize the mess hall menu
body:
“I thought the chief guest meant nation-building, but then he handed me a laminated spreadsheet for next week's curd-rice supply chain,” said a final-year engineering student.

“The speech was very inspiring until the General assigned me the responsibility of tracking every missing teaspoon in the canteen as part of my national duty,” remarked a student council member.

“My son called home to say he’s no longer an electrical engineer but the ‘Chief Responsibility Officer’ for the campus drainage system’s structural integrity,” shared a concerned parent.

“I signed up for a degree in data science, not to be told my primary geopolitical duty is to ensure the hostel geyser functions during the winter months,” noted a confused hostel boarder.

“It’s truly a heavy burden knowing that my contribution to the vision depends entirely on whether I can successfully reconcile the inventory of broken ceiling fans before graduation,” added a graduating mechanical engineer.
caption: IIT graduates are ready to lead the nation, one mess hall inventory at a time. Turns out 'Dhara' is just a code word for 'please fix the water cooler.' #IITConvocation #BharatVision #EngineeringLife (satire)
igHook: Would you trade your degree for the responsibility of managing the campus canteen menu?
imagePrompt: A wide angle shot of a university campus convocation stage with blurred student graduates sitting in rows wearing traditional academic regalia under a bright sunny sky.

sourceHeadline.title: "Bharat is not a geography; it is responsibility": CDS General Raja Subramani shares ‘Dhara’ vision at IIT Roorkee convocation

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 7 stands out for providing a highly specific and grounded absurd scenario—the translation of high-minded 'national vision' speeches into the mundane, infuriating reality of canteen supply chain management. It perfectly balances the absurdity with relatable academic/hostel life, avoiding the repetitive 'everything is a metaphor' tropes found in the other candidates.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses satire to mock bureaucratic incompetence in an academic setting. It does not name any real individuals, avoids protected group targeting, and the image prompt is sufficiently generic.
